subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should this issue be resolved by a diagnostic-only exec warning, or should OpenClaw change gateway-host exec private-LAN reachability semantics?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing diagnostic, but allowing or intentionally blocking private-LAN exec traffic is a product and security-boundary decision that automation should not choose.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94045 while leaving broader private-network access policy to the related security trackers.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI or LaunchAgent reachability parity as the goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Policy Trackers
options.body: Reject the diagnostic-only scope and keep this behavior under the broader private-network policy issues.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94045 while leaving broader private-network access policy to the related security trackers.

likelyOwner.reason: The exec runtime and docs history most consistently routes this security-boundary decision through this owner signal.
